newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan BSPA to tender for 54,000 tonnes soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan BSPA to tender for 54,000 tonnes soybeans.

text.p: The Kaohsiung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association will tender on Wednesday for 54,000 tonnes of U.S., Argentine, Brazilian or Paraguayan soybeans, traders said on Tuesday.
In an unusual twist, the tender specifies the United States as a possible grain source but does not specify shipping dates for any U.S. ports -- making a U.S. purchase all but impossible.

"We will not consider U.S. soybeans because they are more than US$10 higher than the south American grains, particularly the Brazilian beans," a buyer from BSPA member Great Wall Enterprise told Reuters by telephone.

Traders said the tender, if completed with a purchase, could lure other Taiwan soy buyers into the market, particularly the unaffiliated Taichung division of the Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association.

Taiwan's Hui Shung Group also was known to be waiting the right moment to buy 38,500 tonnes of soybeans 16,000 tonnes of corn and was likely to turn to Argentina for the combined shipment, a group buyer said.
The breakfast association's Kaohsiung division consists of Great Wall Enterprise, Ttet Union, President Enterprise and Tai Hwa Oil.
Taiwan interest in Brazilian and Argentine soybeans remains strong as buyers are seeking alternatives to rising U.S. soybean futures prices, traders said.
Taiwan buyers would consider buying south American soybeans if prices were US$10 or more per tonne below U.S. soybeans.
The BSPA's Kaohsiung division was preparing to send delegates to Brazil in April to review its crop planting, silo facilities and port conditions, traders said.
